mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea, Company Registry Office (Deung-gi-so)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issuance by the Korean Company Registry, then notarization by a Korean notary public, followed by apostille certification issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea (Hague Apostille Convention); no consular legalization step is applied because Korea and the destination state are both parties to the Apostille Convention. If the destination state is not an Apostille Convention member, consular legalization is substituted and chaining is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea, Company Registry Office (Deung-gi-so)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issuance by the Korean Company Registry, notarization by a Korean notary public, then apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille member states; for non-member states, consular legalization through the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the relevant Korean consulate or embassy in the destination state, never both sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the parent entity (or sole shareholder resolution if no board yet exists)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Corporate execution under the parent entity's governing law, notarization by a competent notary in the parent entity's jurisdiction, then apostille by the competent national authority designated under the Hague Apostille Convention for Apostille members; for non-members, consular legalization by the destination Korean consulate, with the two processes kept strictly parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporator(s) of the Yuhan Hoesa, authenticated before a Korean notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execution by incorporators, notarization before a Korean notary, and statutory filing with the Korean Commercial Registry; for cross-border evidentiary use, apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs if the receiving country is an Apostille member; otherwise consular legalization exclusively.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank maintaining the corporate account of the parent entity or ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issuance under the bank's official seal, notarization by a notary in the bank's home jurisdiction, apostille by the relevant apostille authority for Apostille Convention states; for non-member states, the bank reference letter must be notarized and then submitted to the destination Korean consulate for consular legalization; no sequential combination of apostille and consular legalization may occur.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent entity's directors and the Korean incorporation agent, certified by competent corporate officers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Corporate certification, notarization of corporate signatories' identities and capacity, apostille by the competent national authority if the origin jurisdiction is an Apostille member; for non-member origin jurisdictions, consular legalization by the Korean embassy or consulate with territorial jurisdiction, and the two methods must never be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The mandatory PEP and sanctions screening protocol requires the Korean incorporation agent and maintainer of the Yuhan Hoesa's corporate records to conduct, before any filing, a risk-calibrated screening of all proposed directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the consolidated list maintained by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit under the Act on Reporting and Using Information Concerning Financial Transactions; the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list; the United Kingdom Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation list; and the Korean government's own autonomous designation list issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and competitive authorities. Screening must be repeated at every material event, including share transfers, director appointments, ledger changes, and name clearance, and each person whose beneficial ownership meets or exceeds 25% of shares or voting rights must be re-verified within the prior 90 days. The protocol must also include a negative news check covering politically exposed persons (PEPs) using at least two independent multilingual data sources, a review of source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation for all capital contributions exceeding USD 10,000 or its won equivalent, and a documented risk rating of low, medium, or high with enhanced due diligence automatically triggered for any PEP, any sanction hit, any adverse media, or any high-risk jurisdiction nexus as identified by the Financial Action Task Force. All screening records, including the exact search date, search terms, database version, and analyst or responsible attorney review, must be retained for at least five years after the termination of the business relationship and, upon request, made available to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit, the registry, and external auditors without the need for a court warrant other than a lawful administrative request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea, Company Registry Online Name Search and Reservation Portal (I-sa-reu and the integrated e-Retention system operated by the Korea Institute of Registered Persons)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean law requires that a Yuhan Hoesa's legal name be stated in Korean characters in all filed constitutional documents. The registered Korean name may include Hangul-only core words; if it includes a term derived from a foreign language, the term must be transliterated into Hangul in accordance with the National Institute of Korean Language's foreign-word transliteration rules, and if the name is rendered in Latin script in parallel, the romanization must follow the Revised Romanization of Korean system approved by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism. The name must include a corporate form identifier such as 'Yuhan Hoesa', 'Yu-han', or 'Ll.C.' that unmistakably denotes a limited liability company. A four-tier naming convention applies: (1) the geographic or brand discriminator, (2) the business purpose or trade name, (3) the product or industry descriptor, and (4) the liability suffix. All name components must satisfy the rule that no two identical legal names exist within the same Company Registry district, and the name clearance search must check homonyms, phonetic equivalents, and close Hangul transliterations to prevent public deception. If the applicant uses a foreign language trade name in contracts or marketing, the foreign name is a secondary trade name only and must not be registered as a substitute for the statutory Korean name unless the foreign-language mark is separately filed as a trademark under the Trademark Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon the receipt of a rejection notice, the applicant must first review the registry's written grounds and, if the grounds are based on a prohibited token or an identical-name conflict, remove the offending component and file a new name reservation using the same online portal. If the applicant believes the rejection is legally erroneous, the applicant's attorney must prepare a written objection addressed to the head of the relevant registry office within 14 days of the rejection date, identifying the legal provision relied upon, attaching the registry's notice, the proposed name in Hangul and romanization, the business registration certificate, and a concise rebuttal of each stated ground. The registry must acknowledge the objection within 7 days and issue a final decision within 30 days. If the registry upholds the rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal to the Supreme Court of Korea Company Registry Administrative Litigation Division within 60 days pursuant to the Administrative Litigation Act; the appeal must include a certified copy of the underlying registry decision, proof that the objection was timely filed, and, where the rejection rests on a construction of the Commercial Act or the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act, a memorandum of law analyzing the competing authorities. During the appeal, the applicant may simultaneously reserve a modified alternative name. If the original name is declared invalid by a final court decision, the applicant must not use the name and should proceed with the modified alternative reservation without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the registered office of a Yuhan Hoesa that will engage in physical designer toy storage, rotocasting, injection molding, or airbrush finishing, because the Korean Commercial Act requires a registered office to be a physically identifiable place where the company's management is actually located and where records may be inspected. The Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education, the Ministry of Economy and Finance, and commercial banks reject mail-only addresses for VAT registration, payroll, customs clearance, and bank account opening in the wholesale/retail and manufacturing sectors. For this ISIC 3240 designer toy business, the Korean local tax office will require a physical place of business for the business registration certificate (sa-eop-ja-deuk-rok), and Korean e-commerce payment rails, including Shopify Payments and Stripe Korea, prohibit virtual office addresses as principal place of business address. At minimum, the company must lease or own either a small production or warehousing facility or a dedicated office suite with the company name on the door, a lease agreement with the actual landlord, a physical reception and delivery capability, and a permanent filing cabinet for VAT, customs, and employment records. A separate mailing address, such as a commercial mail receiving agency, may be used exclusively for correspondence after the physical registered office is established; it may not replace it.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical on-site inspections by Korean municipal district tax offices, the National Tax Service, or the Korea Customs Service are likely. Any registry or tax official may attend the registered address without advance notice during ordinary business hours to confirm that the company is actually operating and that books, VAT invoices, import/export records, and employee records are held there. For a designer blind box business classified under ISIC 3240 and NAICS 339930, the quantified risk of an unannounced inspection within the first twelve months of incorporation is assessed as 35-50%; this risk is elevated if the company imports raw materials, applies for a corporate bank account, receives e-commerce marketplace registrations, or claims input VAT refunds. The district tax office will also perform an address verification site visit when the business registration certificate is issued and usually within 60 days of first VAT filing. To mitigate inspection risk, the company must maintain at the registered office: (1) the original certificate of business registration, (2) the corporate seal certificate, (3) the company ledger and shareholder register, (4) the VAT books and supporting invoices, (5) employment records or outsourcing contracts, and (6) a physical inventory of goods or evidence of warehousing subcontracts; any discrepancy between the registered address and actual warehouse location that is not separately reported to the tax office is treated as a false declaration under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and may lead to a penalty of up to 20% of the relevant tax base or criminal referral.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Government Complex-Sejong, 46 Jungang-ro, Sejong-si, Republic of Korea; online electronic portal is the HomeTax System (hometax.go.kr) for business registration, VAT filing, electronic tax invoices, and corporate tax filings. Korea Customs Service (KCS) is the competent authority for export clearance via the UNI-PASS electronic system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity forming Yuhan Hoesa, the statutory Tax Identification Number is the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN). The mandatory procurement sequence is as follows: 1) incorporate the Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act at the Korean district court registry and obtain the Certificate of Corporate Registration; 2) if the foreign investor makes an FDI or investment report, complete the applicable Foreign Investment Promotion Act filing with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or designated issuing bank; 3) submit the Business Registration Application to the district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered business place, attaching the Certificate of Corporate Registration, articles of incorporation, lease agreement for the registered office, identification documents of the foreign shareholder/director, and evidence of the registered business place; 4) the National Tax Service verifies the application and issues the Business Registration Certificate, and the BRN printed on it simultaneously constitutes the VAT registration number; 5) after issuance, the entity must enrol in the HomeTax System to activate electronic tax invoice issuance and electronic VAT/Corporate Tax filing privileges; 6) for export operations, register and enrol in the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS portal to obtain the customs identifier and link the BRN to export declaration and manifest functions; 7) if the entity is instead a foreign non-resident corporation without a Korean commercial registration but with a place of business, a foreign corporation tax registration must be effected under the Corporate Tax Act, and the NTS may require appointment of a domestic tax representative for procedural notices and filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (a domestic Korean corporation taxed as a separate juridical person; Yuhan Hoesa is subject to Korean corporate income tax on worldwide income, with no pass-through of income or losses to shareholders, plus the local income tax surcharge included in the national corporation tax system).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (the Republic of Korea does not operate a US-style check-the-box entity classification election; a Yuhan Hoesa is by law an entity-level taxpayer and cannot elect pass-through status. Korean tax residence is determined by place of head office or place of effective management, not by shareholder election. Consolidated tax return filing is available only for specially qualifying corporate groups under the Corporate Tax Act and does not change entity-level taxation).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration turnover exemption threshold exists for a business with a Korean place of business; registration is mandatory within 20 days from business commencement. Simplified taxpayer status may apply only to small start-ups meeting statutory turnover thresholds, but a Yuhan Hoesa operating as a domestic corporation is ordinarily required to register as a general VAT taxpayer regardless of initial revenue. Non-resident suppliers of qualifying overseas electronic/digital services have separate VAT registration duties for Korean B2C sales.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory under the VAT Act for all taxable supplies by a registered business to another registered business. The e-tax invoice must be transmitted through the NTS HomeTax System electronic tax invoice service no later than the day following the supply date or the payment date, whichever occurs first, unless a statutory exception applies. HomeTax performs automated validation of the invoice serial number, seller BRN, buyer BRN, supply value, and VAT amount, and cross-matches filed VAT returns against transmitted invoices. API integration is available for high-volume taxpayers to submit invoices in real time. There is no separate physical fiscal stamping duty for general merchandise, but KCS UNI-PASS is the sole national electronic clearance window for export declarations, and approved cash receipt devices are required for qualifying B2C cash transactions to reinforce anti-fraud controls.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the VAT Act, export of goods qualifies for 0% VAT where the taxable person actually exports the designer toy goods from Korea to a foreign destination and substantiates the cross-border movement and the receipt of export proceeds. The supply must be made to a foreign buyer, title and risk must pass offshore under the agreed international commercial terms, and the goods must be removed from Korea through an export declaration in URN system. Qualifying offshore digital or service supplies also may be zero-rated when consumed outside Korea, but physical designer toy merchandise must meet customs export and foreign exchange settlement evidence rules to be treated as an export and to support input VAT refunds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (UNI-PASS electronic export clearance, including export declaration number and date of actual exportation)
Negotiable Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical shipment from Korea to the foreign consignee
Commercial Invoice, Packing List, and purchase order or export contract identifying the designer toy goods, quantities, unit prices, consignor, and consignee

Bank Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation / Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC or Korean foreign exchange settlement equivalent) evidencing collection of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency within the statutory settlement period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service jointly audit export zero-rating claims by matching the export declaration, bill of lading, sales contract, foreign exchange settlement records, supplier payments, and logistics trail. An unsubstantiated export claim is denied at the source, the supply is reclassified as domestically taxable, VAT at 10% is assessed, and the exporter is required to repay any VAT refund previously received. Additional taxes under the Value Added Tax Act may include up to 40% of the relevant supply value for false tax invoices or fraudulent refund claims, plus statutory late payment surcharges and daily interest accruals. Criminal exposure includes investigation and prosecution for foreign exchange violation, false export declaration, and tax evasion, with penalties including imprisonment, fines, forfeiture of export incentives, and retrospective clawback of all customs and VAT benefits for a period determined by the statute of limitations, which is extended in cases of intentional concealment or false documentary evidence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF), through the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and delegated foreign exchange control regulations; designated authorized Korean foreign exchange banks report and settle under the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a largely liberalized current-account convertibility regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, but capital transactions remain subject to declaratory controls rather than unfettered free convertibility. Current-account items, including export and import payments, service fees, royalties, design licensing fees, and trade-related disbursements, are generally convertible into KRW or major foreign currencies through a domestic authorized foreign exchange bank without individual pre-authorization, provided that the underlying contracts, commercial invoices, customs declarations, and tax certificates are genuine. Capital-account items, including inbound equity injections, intercompany loans, and foreign borrowings, must be reported or settled through the FEIS; a non-resident founding a Yuhan Hoesa must file a Foreign Investment Report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) before equity remittances are booked into capital. Profit remittance is permitted after corporate tax clearance, board approval, and dividend declaration, but bank compliance officers will demand audited financial statements, shareholder registry details, withholding tax certificates, and beneficial-ownership evidence. Export receipts must be settled through designated FX banks and FEIS, but Korea does not impose a blanket surrender order requiring conversion into KRW; permitted foreign-currency retention is available for legitimate overseas payments. Overall conversion hurdles are moderate for documented trade and treasury flows, while speculative or structure-driven capital transactions attract heightened regulatory scrutiny.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, export proceeds must be collected through an authorized foreign exchange bank within the statutory settlement period, generally treated as 180 days from the export date for conventional shipment-based receivables, unless prior approval or an extended collection schedule is endorsed by the bank; the export contract, commercial invoice, packing list, and customs export declaration must substantiate each inward remittance. There is no mandatory fixed conversion ratio into KRW for all export receivables; a Yuhan Hoesa may credit foreign currency export receipts into a permitted foreign-currency account, but any foreign currency held beyond legitimate operational needs must be either converted or used for permissible offshore payments, with all balances and settlements declared through the FEIS and reconcilable against the customs report.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to nil for core bank-account replacement; offshore digital EMIs and global challenger banks are not licensed under the Korean Banking Act and cannot lawfully maintain on-demand KRW deposit accounts or provide a Korean settlement address for a Yuhan Hoesa. Fintech platforms such as Toss Business, Kakao Pay Business, and cross-border payment aggregators may provide e-commerce collection, payout processing, or white-label treasury interfaces, but the legal settlement backbone must remain a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank account. Offshore EMIs such as Wise and Payoneer can support collections from global marketplace buyers or Shopify flows, but Korean bank compliance teams will not accept an EMI account as the primary treasury account for a domestic legal entity; all transactions must be routed to an onshore authorized FX bank for FEIS reporting and capital-verification purposes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Tier-1 Korean banks require physical presence of the registered representative director or an authorised domestic financial representative for the initial corporate KYC interview when the Yuhan Hoesa has foreign shareholders. Remote video onboarding is generally not permitted for newly incorporated foreign-owned Korean entities; consular proxy opening is not a recognised standard in Korea. Apostilled powers of attorney may be accepted for execution of documents, but the bank’s AML officer must identify the ultimate beneficial owner and the resident signatory under a face-to-face or a bank-approved video meeting; if the sole foreign director is offshore, a domestically resident director, branch manager, or delegated agent must be appointed for KYC and transaction-verification duties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa where all directors are non-resident and the Korean registered office is only a virtual address, creating UBO and economic-exposure ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide apostilled Certificate of Incorporation, Korean Business Registration Certificate, company register excerpt, full share registry showing each shareholder’s beneficial percentage, notarised shareholder resolution for account opening, passport copies, foreign corporate registry extract or ownership chart, sworn source-of-funds declaration, and a executed registered-office lease or business-secretariat agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Designer blind-box toy business combines high volume low-value e-commerce export with intercompany licensing or royalty flows, raising trade-based money-laundering and transfer-mispricing red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present a commercial-substance file with design copyright and trademark registrations, trademark assignment or licensing agreements, injection-moulding and PVC/vinyl production contracts, third-party quality-control inspection certificates, Shopify and Stripe payout logs, custom declaration ELPASS export records, courier air waybill tracking summaries, product catalogue, and management accounts for the first two operating quarters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity funding and recurring foreign affiliate payments originating from jurisdictions perceived as high-risk or from shareholders without bankable financial history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the Foreign Investment Report and foreign exchange bank receipt certificate, shareholder bank reference letter, audited financial statements or tax returns of the parent entity, certified copies of intercompany goods-supply and licensing contracts, arm’s-length transfer-pricing opinion, customs valuation certificates, board resolutions approving all fund movements, and proof that all Korean withholding tax and corporate tax accruals have been filed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between claimed e-commerce distribution model and fragmented settlement rails, prepaid cards, digital wallets, or split-payments leading to incomplete transaction monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a treasury and settlement policy document, merchant agreements with Stripe or Shopify Payments, commission and payout delay schedules, chargeback and refund reconciliation reports, daily payout summaries, inventory purchase orders with VAT invoices, warehouse and fulfilment records, and a documented value-chain dossier from raw PVC pellet procurement through rotocasting, airbrushing, final assembly, blind-box packing, and cross-border shipment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign shareholder equity for the Yuhan Hoesa should be remitted via SWIFT MT103 after filing the Foreign Investment Report under FIPA and obtaining acknowledgment from the designated Korean foreign exchange bank; the MT103 narrative must clearly state Direct Investment / Equity Capital Injection / Korea FIPA Declaration, and the Korean bank must receive the foreign exchange purchase settlement code corresponding to direct investment equity. The remittance is credited to a Capital Escrow Account, converted to KRW under bank-controlled spot rate, and the paid-in capital is verified by a certified public accountant against bank statements, share issuance, and the Foreign Investment Registration certificate; any mislabelled ordinary remittance risks FEIS reporting penalties or reclassification as a shareholder loan, both of which could disturb capital verification and dividend repatriation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For manufacturing, moulding, paint, packaging, and logistics suppliers located outside Korea, use SWIFT MT103 wire transfers with the appropriate Foreign Exchange Transactions Act purpose code and an underlying import invoice or purchase order; for larger production lots, use irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit issued by a Korean bank with documents drawn against bills of lading, commercial invoices, packing lists, and certificates of quality; Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) may be used for open-account trade with established counterparties. Each disbursement must be matched with the approved customs import declaration, reported in FEIS, and reconciled against the invoice denomination and bank settlement records, with no cash payments or unofficial prepayment channels.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD FX forward contracts executed with authorised Korean foreign exchange banks under the Real Demand Principle, requiring documented export receivables or import payables
Onshore KRW/USD FX swaps for natural cash-flow matching of export proceeds settled in USD against KRW operating costs and payables

Cross-currency swaps in KRW/USD to hedge intercompany loans, paid-in-capital funding, and long-term trade credit lines, provided the notional is supported by a real foreign-exchange exposure and not speculative

KRW non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible as an onshore hedging instrument for a Korean-domiciled corporate treasury; offshore NDF usage may only be referenced for mark-to-market analysis and cannot be booked on the Yuhan Hoesa bank account without specific Bank of Korea approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Final Return and Tax Settlement Package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of Korea via HomeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, no later than March 31 of the following year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within three months after the fiscal year-end; a one-month extension is available upon prior application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the corporate income tax return attracts an additional tax of 20% of the final corporate income tax payable; under-reporting attracts 10% of the under-reported tax, rising to 40% for fraudulent concealment; unpaid tax accrues a daily delinquency charge of 0.03% from the statutory due date until full payment; persistent non-filing and non-payment over 12 months can trigger asset seizure, refusal to accept tax invoices, deletion of the business registration with the local tax office, and eventual commercial registry strike-off procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government office (si/gun/gu) of the head office via the WeTax local tax e-filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the central corporate income tax return is due, i.e., April 30 for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Local Tax Act imposes a daily delinquency surcharge of 0.03% on unpaid local corporate income tax, together with a 20% non-filing additional tax and a 10% under-reporting additional tax (40% for deliberate concealment); unresolved delinquency can lead to seizures, compulsory collection, deletion of the local business registration, and forced shutdown of taxable activity, which can ultimately support a commercial registry removal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value Added Tax Preliminary Return for January 1 to March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By April 25 of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment of VAT attracts a daily surcharge of 0.03% of the unpaid VAT and a statutory additional tax of 20% of the VAT payable for non-filing (40% for fraudulent refund claims); repeated violations lead to tax office business suspension, bank account seizure, deletion of the VAT business registration, and personal liability of the representative for unpaid VAT when the company is found to be delinquent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value Added Tax Final Return for April 1 to June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By July 25 of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment of VAT attracts a daily surcharge of 0.03% of the unpaid VAT and a statutory additional tax of 20% of the VAT payable for non-filing (40% for fraudulent refund claims); repeated violations lead to tax office business suspension, bank account seizure, deletion of the VAT business registration, and personal liability of the representative for unpaid VAT when the company is found to be delinquent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value Added Tax Preliminary Return for July 1 to September 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By October 25 of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment of VAT attracts a daily surcharge of 0.03% of the unpaid VAT and a statutory additional tax of 20% of the VAT payable for non-filing (40% for fraudulent refund claims); repeated violations lead to tax office business suspension, bank account seizure, deletion of the VAT business registration, and personal liability of the representative for unpaid VAT when the company is found to be delinquent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value Added Tax Final Return for October 1 to December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment of VAT attracts a daily surcharge of 0.03% of the unpaid VAT and a statutory additional tax of 20% of the VAT payable for non-filing (40% for fraudulent refund claims); repeated violations lead to tax office business suspension, bank account seizure, deletion of the VAT business registration, and personal liability of the representative for unpaid VAT when the company is found to be delinquent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting of Members and Approval of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate head office for the minute book; Commercial Registration Court of the District Court where the registered office is located if any registration consequence arises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of each fiscal year, i.e., by March 31 for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Commercial Act does not automatically dissolve the company for a missed meeting, but any member or director may apply to the court to compel a lawful meeting; directors who intentionally fail to convene the annual members meeting are exposed to an administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million, and any resolution adopted outside a lawfully convened general meeting is void; continuing failure can be used by the tax authorities and creditors as evidence of abandonment, supporting court-led strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service through DART and National Tax Service through the corporate income tax filing package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If the Yuhan Hoesa is subject to mandatory external audit, the corporate income tax return including the audited financial statements must be filed by March 31, and the audit report must be submitted to DART within two weeks after the ordinary general meeting approving the financial statements, normally by April 14 for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Act on External Audit of Joint-Stock Companies etc., failure to file the statutory audit report, or failure to appoint a registered external auditor, can result in administrative fines of up to KRW 10 million; false or defective audit filings can lead to criminal referral, regulatory designation as an audit non-compliant company, a mandatory special tax audit by the National Tax Service, and enhanced reputational sanctions; it does not by itself trigger strike-off, but the underlying financial statement filing failure will do so through the tax delinquency route.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Joint-Stock Companies etc. and the Commercial Act, a Yuhan Hoesa (Korean limited liability company) is legally required to appoint an independent certified CPA auditor and undergo an independent annual audit if: (i) total assets at the end of the prior fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 8.9 million); or (ii) total assets equal or exceed KRW 7 billion and the company has annual revenue equal to or greater than KRW 10 billion; or (iii) total assets equal or exceed KRW 7 billion and the average number of regular employees during the fiscal year equals or exceeds 100; or (iv) the company is designated as a public-interest company under Article 1-4 of the same Act and total assets equal or exceed KRW 5 billion; or (v) the company voluntarily elects external audit or is required by a lender, investor, or foreign parent for consolidated reporting. Below these thresholds, no independent statutory CPA audit is mandatory for the Yuhan Hoesa, but the company must still prepare reliable financial statements and file a corporate tax reconciliation schedule with the National Tax Service.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean-Adopted International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are mandatory for listed companies and public-interest entities; unlisted companies such as a privately held Yuhan Hoesa may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP), including the Accounting Standards for Non-Listed Entities and the Korean SME accounting standards issued by the Korean Accounting Standards Board. Regardless of the framework chosen, financial statements must be prepared on the accrual basis, denominated in KRW, with comparative prior-year figures, and the corporate income tax return must be reconciled from accounting profit to taxable income under the Korean Corporate Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Korean Commercial Act does not require a Yuhan Hoesa to file a standalone annual UBO confirmation return with the commercial registry. Instead, the statutory register of members must at all times be kept up to date at the registered office and must show the name, address, contribution quota, and date of acquisition of every member. Whenever a membership interest or share quota is transferred, the transfer is effective against third parties only after entry in the register of members, and any change requiring a commercial registration, including changes in directors, members, or the registered office, must be filed with the competent Commercial Registration Court within 30 days after the effective date of the corporate resolution or transaction. For anti-money laundering compliance, the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information requires the company to identify and verify its beneficial owners whenever it opens a bank account, establishes a business relationship, or when a reportable ownership change occurs; financial institutions may require annual reconfirmation of UBO data, and failure to update beneficial ownership information within 30 days of the actual change can expose the company to administrative fines and witness the loss of the transfer's legal opposability to bona fide third parties.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 1,200 per year for a standard corporate secretarial agent with a physical registered office address in Seoul or a major Korean business centre; premium business district or foreign-facing office addresses may range from KRW 1,500,000 to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 1,100 - USD 3,700) per year
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,500 - USD 22,000 for a typical non-listed Korean Yuhan Hoesa with ordinary designer-toy merchandising revenue where mandatory audit applies; USD 25,000 - USD 50,000 where the company operates as part of a cross-border designer-toy group requiring K-IFRS consolidated audit, intercompany review, or foreign parent reporting

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: National Corporate Tax at 10% for taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 20% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, and 22% above KRW 20 billion; adding the 10% Local Income Tax surcharge gives a combined top marginal rate of 24.2%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general patent box exists in Korea, but a Yuhan Hoesa can reduce effective tax through the Special Tax Treatment Control Law R&D credits (25%-50% of qualifying design and prototyping expenditure), SME reduced rates, foreign-investment tax holidays for advanced technology facilities, and expensing of molds and tooling; revenue derived from non-Korean online sales may be enhanced by foreign tax credits and VAT export zero-rating.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate income tax is declared on the Corporate Tax Return for Tax Base and Tax Calculation (Form 111) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal; supporting schedules include financial statements, tax reconciliation schedules, foreign tax credit schedule, transfer pricing disclosure schedules and the Local Income Tax return for the 10% urban/rural local corporate surtax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; a calendar-year entity must file by March 31, and a one-month extension is available by prior application through HomeTax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification block: legal name, business registration number, fiscal year, head office and factory address, KSIC industry code, shareholder list, stock ownership percentages, foreign shareholder nationality and place of effective management.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean Standard Industrial Classification code corresponding to ISIC 3240 for designer blind box toy manufacturing; identify every non-resident shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner, state each foreign jurisdiction of tax residence, and disclose the treaty country relied upon for dividend or royalty withholding relief so that the Korean filing position is consistent with DTA forms attached outside the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit and loss statement: gross sales, returns and allowances, cost of goods sold, inventory valuation, payroll, rent, shipping, payment processing fees, advertising, depreciation, royalties, interest and other expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bring into gross revenue all sales settled through Shopify Payments, Stripe and local POS terminals when control and risk pass to the customer; do not defer cross-border designer toy sales merely because collection occurs through a foreign payment gateway; deduct royalties and management fees paid to non-residents only when Economic Substance documentation, source evidence and arm's length supporting files are available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from book income to taxable income: add backs for nondeductible expenses, penalties, excess entertainment, bad debts owed by shareholders, non-statutory reserves; deductions for tax-exempt income, reserve reversals and net operating loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back payments to non-resident parties where withholding was not made, where a foreign tax invoice was not issued, or where the expense lacks a valid DTA-supported royalty license; deduct only the statutory five-year loss carryforward and document the loss year, amount and ownership continuity; a Yuhan Hoesa with foreign controlling shareholders must be prepared to demonstrate that transfer pricing adjustments have not been omitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base computation and national corporate tax calculation: application of progressive rates to the final positive taxable income, including minimum tax computations and any business year splitting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean redomestic Yuhan Hoesa is subject to worldwide income tax as a domestic corporation; declare foreign-source manufacturing royalties and overseas e-commerce revenue in the tax base unless a Korean tax treaty or domestic exclusion applies; ensure that any permanent establishment outside Korea is attributed only its OECD-compliant profits and that Korean central costs are not overstated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits, exemptions, and reliefs: R&D credit, SME tax reduction, temporary investment credit, indirect foreign tax credit, foreign dividend deduction and foreign employment income categories.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim R&D credits for mold creation, blind box design prototyping and airbrush finishing trials; attach foreign tax credit schedules for withholding taxes suffered abroad; treaty-sourced income must be allocated consistently with Korean tax return line items so that double-counting of foreign tax credits is avoided and non-resident shareholders cannot separately claim benefits already absorbed by the LLC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Special adjustments and anti-abuse computations: thin capitalization, deemed dividends, loan equity recharacterization, excessive debt or loss assumptions, and general anti-avoidance rule adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize that interest on a foreign controlling shareholder loan exceeding Korea s thin capitalization ratio may be recharacterized as a dividend, increasing the Korean tax base and outbound withholding obligation; also disclose any taxpayer-initiated transfer pricing adjustment before the NTS audit so that a 20% penalty on the adjusted amount is avoided.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party cross-border transaction schedule: intercompany purchases, sales, royalties, service fees, loan balances, cost sharing, profit contributions and transfer pricing method applied to each category.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Local File must be substantiated where controlled foreign transactions reach KRW 5 billion, and a Master File/CbC report obligation is tested against KRW 100 billion consolidated group revenue; enter the exact OECD method used (CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM or profit split), attach functional and risk analyses for the Korean factory, and flag any use of low-tax jurisdictions for treasury or brand holding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax and non-resident payment declaration: summary of outbound dividends, interest, royalties, technical service fees, director fees and other domestic-source income paid to foreign persons.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute statutory aggregate withholding of 22% (20% national plus 2% local surtax) on dividends, interest and royalties unless a Korea DTA reduction is documented; attach the foreign shareholder Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership declaration and treaty application record; if the LLC has failed to withhold, the NTS may deny the expense deduction, assess the payor as responsible party and apply penalties to the responsible director.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax payable and payment summary: national corporate tax, 10% Local Income Tax surcharge, prepayments, tax credits against prepayments and overdue interest or additional tax from the prior amended returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the Local Income Tax surcharge is computed only on the final national corporate tax after credits; retain proof of electronic payment through HomeTax; for dividend remittances, remit the reduced or statutory withholding within the statutory deadline and preserve the bank evidence to prove that Korean tax was actually borne before claiming treaty credit abroad.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and insufficient remittance attract additional tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes of 10% for ordinary negligent underreporting and up to 40% for fraudulent omission, plus daily overdue charges; failure to submit transfer pricing documentation can be penalized up to KRW 70 million, and NTS can reassess all related-party prices and impose a 20% penalty on adjusted taxable income; deliberate concealment of designer toy revenues exposed through Shopify, Stripe or POS output is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine up to three times the tax evaded, while major delinquents are blacklisted, denied departure from Korea and subjected to asset seizure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate statutory rate on outbound dividends (20% national withholding under the Corporate Tax Act plus 2% Local Income Tax surtax); Korea DTA rates for dividends are normally 0%-15% depending on shareholder ownership percentage, treaty partner and beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply DTA relief, the foreign payee and Korean paying Yuhan Hoesa must file the Korean application for withholding tax reduction/exemption before or at the time of remittance through HomeTax, attaching: (i) a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority; (ii) a beneficial ownership certificate identifying the actual owner and the full payment chain, with confirmation that no conduit arrangement exists; (iii) evidence that the foreign recipient has no Korean permanent establishment to which the dividend, interest or royalty is effectively connected; (iv) board resolutions and financial statements proving distributable profits; and (v) for royalties, the license agreement, trademark/patent registration and a functional analysis showing the Korean entity s Core Income-Generating Activities. The NTS may deny relief where substance is lacking, and the paying company must withhold the full 22% until the treaty claim is administratively accepted.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties have a statutory withholding burden of 22% (20% national withholding plus 2% local surtax), commonly reduced to 10%-15% under Korean DTA where the recipient is beneficial owner and no Korean PE exists; interest has the same 22% statutory burden, with treaty rates generally 10%-15%, although interest paid to a foreign controlling shareholder may be recharacterized as a deemed dividend under thin capitalization rules and thereby lose treaty protection on the excess portion.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where the aggregate value of cross-border transactions with specially related foreign parties equals or exceeds KRW 5 billion in a business year; Master File and Country-by-Country Reporting obligations arise when the multinational group s consolidated revenue equals or exceeds KRW 100 billion; NTS may nevertheless request lower-threshold documentation in audit where there is evidence of non-arm s length pricing.
